articles.title: Sociable: Meta says its expanded processing capacity is driving ad results
articles.summary: Meta detailed how AI upgrades to its ad delivery infrastructure are improving advertiser performance, announcing on Oct. 28 that Q2 2026 improvements to its ads ranking system increased Facebook ad clicks by 8.3% and conversions by 15.7%. Key drivers include an upgraded Andromeda ranking model that now evaluates a broader range of product matches against user interests, the Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM) processing more engagement signals for relevance, and GenRecs improving matching even for new ads lacking engagement history. In Q3, further Andromeda refinements lifted Facebook conversions by 1.4%, while newly launched generative retrieval on Facebook Feed added nearly 2% more conversions in targeted segments. Separately, Meta said its AI business assistant, being rolled out more broadly to advertisers, is driving 5% more conversions at equal cost. Partnership ads, which let brands collaborate with creators, grew over 97% year-over-year in Q3 and now exceed a $15 billion annual revenue run-rate. Meta is also building checkout functionality into AI agents like Muse to enable in-stream purchases, reflecting broader investment in data-center capacity to fuel these targeting improvements.
articles.li_summary: Meta reported that AI-driven improvements to its ad ranking systems boosted Facebook ad clicks by 8.3% and conversions by 15.7% in Q2 2026, with further Q3 gains from Andromeda and generative retrieval updates.

articles.title: Disney plans TikTok Shop holiday experience with over 20 brands
articles.summary: Disney is launching its first TikTok Shop Super Brand Day, running Nov. 4-10, as part of a broader "Make the Holidays Magic" holiday campaign amplified through paid media and creator content. The event combines Disney Store merchandise with offerings from more than 20 partner brands, including Old Navy, Crocs, Corkcicle, ColourPop, Touchland, Kyte Baby, FHI Heat, Girls Crew and PopSockets, each featuring Disney-themed collections spanning home goods, toys, beauty, fashion and accessories tied to Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Star Wars properties. Two products, a Darth on a Hearth collectible and a Loungefly holiday mini backpack, will debut exclusively on TikTok Shop before becoming available on Disney's own website. The push builds on Disney's August content-sharing partnership with TikTok and reflects rising trust in the platform's shopping tools, with GlobalData research showing 67% of U.S. consumers trust major brands equally or more when discovered via TikTok Shop versus other platforms, rising to 82% among 18-24 year-olds. Emarketer projects TikTok Shop's U.S. sales will grow 48% in 2026 to $23.4 billion, following recent debuts from Sephora, Best Buy and others.
articles.li_summary: Disney will host its first TikTok Shop "Super Brand Day" from Nov. 4-10, uniting Disney Store products with over 20 partner brands like Old Navy, Crocs and ColourPop for holiday shopping.

articles.title: What marketers should know about the legal risks of algorithmic pricing
articles.summary: A guest op-ed by Simpson Thacher & Bartlett partner Laura Brett warns marketers that algorithmic pricing — charging different customers different prices using data like browsing history, location or loyalty status — now carries serious legal exposure beyond new pricing laws, including false-advertising claims. New York's pending One Fair Price Act, awaiting Hochul's signature or veto by Dec. 31, would broadly ban individualized pricing across most industries. The piece cites Instacart's December 2025 controversy, where Consumer Reports found some shoppers paying up to 23% more for identical items, prompting the company to halt the practice while New York AG Letitia James demanded pricing records. Brett distinguishes "dynamic pricing" (same price for all customers, varying by time or demand) from riskier "surveillance" or "personalized" pricing based on individual data. More than 20 states have pending bills, the FTC has drafted policy guidance, and a House Oversight probe has targeted Uber and Lyft. New Jersey allows private lawsuits with treble damages. Brett advises marketers to audit data inputs, map pricing practices by jurisdiction, and involve legal counsel before deploying new pricing tools.
articles.li_summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul faces a Dec. 31 deadline to sign or veto the One Fair Price Act, a sweeping ban on individualized pricing, as regulators nationwide intensify scrutiny of algorithmic and surveillance pricing practices used by marketers.

articles.title: Pinterest reports solid user growth in Q3
articles.summary: Pinterest's Q3 2026 earnings, released Oct. 29, revealed 21 million new global monthly active users compared to Q2, bringing total MAU to 661 million. Notably, European user growth is recovering after a year of stagnation and decline, while 17 million of the new users came from "Rest of World" markets outside the U.S. and Europe. Gen Z now makes up 57% of Pinterest's audience, and engagement is climbing among U.S. and Canada users across search, board creation, and outbound clicks. Revenue reached $1.17 billion, a 12% year-over-year increase, with U.S./Canada revenue up 14%, though international growth was dampened by European regulatory changes affecting cross-border sales. Pinterest is expanding its programmatic ad buying globally and improving AI-driven ad targeting using broader signal integration. The company is also boosting creator monetization, allowing brands to sponsor creator Pins and launching a Roku TV show featuring in-app products, alongside new visual search ads introduced last month. With over 80 billion monthly searches, Pinterest continues prioritizing AI-powered discovery while facing growing user concerns about AI-generated content flooding Pins.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest's Q3 2026 results show 661 million global monthly active users after adding 21 million in the quarter, with revenue hitting $1.17 billion, up 12% year-over-year.

articles.title: YouTube subscriptions are rising as more users turn to connected TV
articles.summary: Alphabet's fiscal Q3 2026 results show YouTube's ad revenue growth cooling to 9% year-over-year, reaching $11.2 billion, down from 13% growth in Q2, even as subscription revenue accelerates. YouTube Music and Premium subscriptions hit 150 million, up from 100 million in early 2024, helping drive an 11% rise in Google's overall subscription revenue. Much of this momentum stems from connected TV viewing, with YouTube now ranked the top U.S. streaming platform per Nielsen's August 2026 Gauge report. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler noted that Living Room, YouTube's CTV experience, now generates more than one-third of total YouTube ad revenue. The platform is also expanding creator monetization, with over three million creators in its partnership program and 1.3 million channels enrolled in shopping features, plus a new Amazon affiliate partnership letting U.S. creators tag products in videos, Shorts, and livestreams. On the AI front, Schindler highlighted new generative tools in YouTube Studio and a conversational editing assistant for Shorts, with 61% of recent video uploaders expressing interest in using AI to insert themselves into content.
articles.li_summary: Alphabet's Q3 FY2026 earnings show YouTube ad revenue growth slowing to 9% year-over-year to $11.2 billion, while YouTube Music and Premium subscriptions climbed to 150 million, up from 100 million in early 2024.

articles.title: Threads tests smaller group sharing option
articles.summary: Threads is trialing a new feature called Threads Friends, modeled closely on Instagram's Close Friends tool, which lets users build a smaller, private group of up to 50 selected connections to share posts with instead of broadcasting to their entire follower base. Once someone creates a Threads Friends list, they get the option to publish updates visible only to that group rather than the public feed. Threads has confirmed that people added to a list will see a "Threads Friends" label on relevant posts, making them aware they've been included, and that likes or replies from other members of the list will be visible to everyone else in the group, showing usernames and interactions. The feature is currently being tested only with users in Ireland, Italy and Japan, though anyone from anywhere in the world can be added to a Friends list regardless of their location. The move reflects a broader industry shift away from public, broadcast-style posting toward smaller, curated sharing spaces as platforms look for new ways to boost user engagement.
articles.li_summary: Threads is testing "Threads Friends," a Close Friends-style feature letting users share posts with up to 50 selected connections instead of all followers, piloted in Ireland, Italy and Japan.

articles.title: Disney plans TikTok Shop holiday experience with over 20 brands
articles.summary: Disney is making its TikTok Shop debut with a Super Brand Day event running November 4-10 as part of its "Make the Holidays Magic" holiday campaign, marking the company's first time using the platform's dedicated shopping feature for a major seasonal push. The event will showcase Disney Store merchandise alongside offerings from more than 20 licensing partners, including Old Navy, Crocs, Corkcicle, ColourPop, Touchland, Kyte Baby, FHI Heat, Girls Crew and PopSockets, spanning categories like toys, beauty, home goods and fashion tied to Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Star Wars properties. Two items, a Darth Vader-themed "Darth on a Hearth" collectible and a Loungefly holiday mini backpack, will be sold exclusively through the Disney Store's TikTok Shop before becoming available on Disney's own website. The campaign will be supported by paid media and creator content. Disney Consumer Products SVP Liz Shortreed framed the move as adapting to how fans now discover and purchase branded merchandise. The push follows an August content partnership between Disney and TikTok, and comes as TikTok Shop's U.S. sales are projected by Emarketer to grow 48% in 2026 to $23.4 billion, with GlobalData finding 67% of U.S. consumers trust brands more when encountered there.
articles.li_summary: Disney will launch its first TikTok Shop Super Brand Day from Nov. 4-10, featuring Disney Store products and over 20 partner brands like Old Navy, Crocs and ColourPop, plus two TikTok-exclusive holiday items.

articles.title: What marketers should know about the legal risks of algorithmic pricing
articles.summary: Marketers face mounting legal exposure around algorithmic pricing, where software sets different prices for different customers based on signals like browsing history, location, or loyalty status, rather than simple dynamic pricing that charges everyone the same fluctuating rate. New York Governor Kathy Hochul must decide by December 31 whether to sign the One Fair Price Act, a broad ban on individualized pricing across most industries, reflecting a surge of similar bills pending in more than 20 states. In December 2025, Consumer Reports found Instacart charging some shoppers up to 23% more for identical items; the company halted the practice, but New York Attorney General Letitia James still demanded its pricing records. A House Oversight committee has also sought records from Uber and Lyft, while the FTC has drafted guidance on when personalized pricing becomes deceptive or unfair. States vary widely, some banning the practice in grocery and retail, others requiring disclosures like New York's algorithm-pricing notices, with New Jersey allowing private lawsuits and treble damages. Attorney Laura Brett advises marketers to audit which data feeds pricing decisions, map where personalized pricing occurs, and involve legal counsel before deploying new pricing tools, since loyalty discounts carry lower risk than targeting by device or location.
articles.li_summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul faces a Dec. 31 deadline to sign or veto the One Fair Price Act, a sweeping ban on individualized algorithmic pricing, as regulators nationwide intensify scrutiny of personalized pricing practices following Instacart's December 2025 pricing controversy.

articles.title: What influencer fatigue says about creator-driven marketing’s next phase
articles.summary: A Nantucket artisan shop's "no influencers" sign went viral this July, sparking debate over whether influencer culture has worn out its welcome, and reigniting discussion of so-called "influencer fatigue." Yet data suggests the channel remains strong: 72% of young consumers follow influencers, 58% have bought products based on creator endorsements, and nearly 80% of brands work with one to ten influencers at a time, according to the Association of National Advertisers, which projects U.S. creator-economy ad spend will hit $43.9 billion by 2026. Over 80% of marketers plan to boost influencer budgets within a year, per Sprout Social, even as costs rise through pricier PR packages, brand trips and fees, plus new tools like Meta's creator-matching suite. More than half of creators with 500,000-plus followers report friction between brand demands and audience expectations. Whisker CMO Hew Loyd, who manages influencer relationships in-house (done by only 16% of marketers), says fatigue is real in person but more nuanced online, as brands shift toward niche-fit over follower count, now ranked the least important selection factor.
articles.li_summary: Despite viral "no influencers" backlash like a Nantucket shop's sign, 72% of young consumers still follow influencers and U.S. creator-economy ad spend is projected to hit $43.9 billion in 2026, per the ANA.

articles.title: Meta says its expanded processing capacity is driving ad results
articles.summary: Meta detailed how AI-driven improvements to its ad delivery infrastructure are boosting advertiser performance across its platforms. In Q3, Andromeda improvements added a further 1.4% conversion increase, while generative retrieval launched on Facebook Feed lifted conversions nearly 2% in targeted segments. Separately, Meta said its AI business assistant, still expanding to more advertisers, is generating 5% more conversions at equal cost. Partnership ads, which let brands collaborate with creators, grew over 97% year-over-year in Q3 and now exceed a $15 billion annual revenue run-rate. Meta is also building checkout functionality into AI agents like Muse to enable in-stream purchases.
articles.li_summary: Meta announced Oct. 28 that Q2 2026 ad ranking upgrades boosted Facebook ad clicks by 8.3% and conversions by 15.7%, while its AI business assistant now drives 5% more conversions at the same cost.

articles.title: Reddit introduces For You feed
articles.summary: Reddit is introducing a new For You feed powered by algorithmic recommendations, designed to help users discover new subreddits and discussions beyond the communities they've already joined. This feed will sit alongside the existing Following feed, which shows updates from communities users already follow, giving people a clearer split between discovery and catch-up browsing. Notably, For You has been placed in the primary tab position as Reddit pushes discovery, though it won't be the default view—the app will instead open to whichever feed a user last viewed. Reddit says the change uses its engagement and audience data to predict content users might find interesting, framing it as part of ongoing experiments to make the platform more valuable, with future plans including more navigation options and controls like hiding posts or flagging unwanted content. The rollout will happen globally over the coming weeks. The move comes amid broader industry debate over algorithmic feeds' risks and benefits, and growing calls for platforms to offer non-algorithmic, chronological feed opt-outs.
articles.li_summary: Reddit is rolling out a new algorithm-driven For You feed alongside its existing Following feed, letting users choose between discovering new subreddits or catching up on joined communities, with global rollout over the next few weeks.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse AI agents are now available to users in Singapore
articles.summary: Meta has launched its Muse AI agent in Singapore, marking the first expansion of the tool into Southeast Asia after its U.S. and Canada debut last month, where it hit 10 million downloads within its first 30 days. In Singapore, Muse connects to personal apps like Gmail, Google Calendar and Instagram to manage email, scheduling and saved content, while also linking to local partners including Shopee, Lazada, Grab, GrabMart, Grab Dine Out, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, Klook, Trip.com and ShopBack to help users compare prices, book travel, order food and earn cashback. The move follows Zuckerberg's comments on Meta's Q3 earnings call that shopping is Muse's top use case, with over 25% of users seeking deals or making purchases averaging more than $200 each — a trend Meta likely hopes to amplify in Singapore's e-commerce-heavy market. The expansion reflects Meta's broader push to embed AI into daily routines as it tries to justify AI spending that could eventually top $1 trillion, with Muse positioned as a potential key driver toward profitability.
articles.li_summary: Meta expanded its Muse AI assistant to Singapore, its first Southeast Asia launch, adding local app integrations with Shopee, Grab, Lazada, Singapore Airlines, Agoda, Klook, Trip.com and ShopBack for shopping, dining and travel tasks.

articles.title: Edits gets new Halloween-themed options
articles.summary: Meta rolled out a fresh batch of updates to its Edits video editing app, led by Halloween-themed creative tools including new spooky fonts, sound effects, animations, and 13 additional text animation styles for seasonal content. The update also introduces beat-synced effects like flashing lights and zoom transitions that automatically sync to a clip's music or audio. Caption tools got an upgrade too, with new styling options and the ability to bulk-edit captions across a project. On the technical side, Meta added automated color adjustment to simplify brightness and color balancing, along with the option to boost individual clip volume up to 150% within a project. The carousel editor, previously limited to iOS, is now available on Android devices. Edits also debuted a custom filter created in partnership with Nigerian musician Arya Starr. With these additions, Edits continues evolving into a comprehensive video creation studio, and Meta has confirmed a desktop version is coming soon, which should further expand creators' editing capabilities beyond mobile devices.
articles.li_summary: Meta updated its Edits video app with Halloween-themed fonts, sound effects, and 13 new text animations, plus automated color adjustment, 150% clip volume boost, and Android carousel editing support.

articles.title: YouTube adds microdrama subscriptions
articles.summary: YouTube announced plans to deepen its investment in microdramas, the short, serialized vertical video format that generated more than 6.5 billion views within the app during the first half of 2026, a jump of over 50% compared to the previous year, with particularly strong growth in the Asia Pacific region. To support creators financially, YouTube is revamping the mobile viewing experience in the coming weeks so viewers can join a channel membership and continue watching members-only episodes without exiting the content, building on last month's MadeOn announcement of Shorts Series for organizing episodic content into seasons. The platform also highlighted how auto-translation tools, including multi-language audio, AI-generated subtitles, and localized metadata, help creators reach international audiences without dubbing costs, noting that a series filmed in Tokyo or Seoul can attract viewers in Brazil. YouTube shared data showing 40% of views and 30% of clicks happen more than 30 days post-launch, meaning early episodes keep generating ad revenue long-term. Keys to success include quick emotional hooks, vertical-first filming, frequent uploads, relatable storylines, and interactive formats where audiences influence plot direction, creating fresh marketing and product placement opportunities.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is streamlining in-app channel memberships for microdrama episodes on mobile, letting viewers subscribe without leaving the video, after the format hit 6.5 billion views in H1 2026, up over 50% year-over-year.

articles.title: Meta adds individual performance data for ad creative
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out a new "Breakdown" element within its Ads Manager platform that gives advertisers visibility into how individual creative components of their ads are performing, rather than just viewing aggregate results. Selecting the "Media" option reveals how specific images and videos performed as standalone assets, while a separate view shows performance by text variation, helping marketers identify which specific creative elements are driving results. The tool has some gaps: ads using multi-post formats like "Show as collection" or "Show as carousel" are excluded from this breakdown, and it doesn't provide insight for certain custom conversion actions such as "Donate" or "Subscribe." This update follows Meta's move last week to let advertisers assign specific audience targeting to individual creative pieces within a campaign, even as the company simultaneously stripped away other manual targeting controls, including detailed targeting options, to push advertisers toward relying more heavily on its AI-driven ad delivery system for audience selection and optimization.
articles.li_summary: Meta added a new "Breakdown" feature in Ads Manager that lets advertisers see individual performance data for each image, video, and text variation within a single ad, excluding carousel and collection formats.

articles.title: LinkedIn launches data insights hub
articles.summary: LinkedIn has relaunched its Economic Graph insights platform under the name LinkedIn Pulse, reusing a moniker previously tied to its 2015 creator publishing tool. The revamped hub pulls data from LinkedIn's 1.4 billion members, 71 million companies and 42,000 tracked skills to help businesses, governments and individuals spot emerging work trends and opportunities. CMO Jessica Jensen said the platform draws on LinkedIn's in-house economists, who already advise companies, policymakers and media on global labor market shifts, and is now being opened up more broadly so users can make better decisions about careers, teams or business strategy. As part of the relaunch, LinkedIn is partnering with journalists, including Scalable founder Kaya Yurieff, to produce deeper analysis on specific economic topics such as AI's impact on jobs. While the insights could prove useful for tracking workforce and market shifts, the reused Pulse name may cause some confusion given its earlier association with LinkedIn's long-form content publishing feature launched a decade ago, which has since faded from prominence.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn has rebranded its Economic Graph as LinkedIn Pulse, a data hub drawing on 1.4 billion members, 71 million companies and 42,000 skills to track shifting labor market opportunities.

articles.title: LinkedIn tests simplified UI
articles.summary: LinkedIn has begun rolling out a test version of a simplified navigation experience across desktop and mobile, aimed at reducing menu clutter and better reflecting how users actually engage with the app. On desktop, several previously separate function menus have been merged, with a "Profile" tab now housing analytics, saved posts and settings, while a new "More" tab consolidates access to puzzle games, news, groups, events, newsletters and video. The mobile app's lower navigation bar mirrors these same consolidated listings. LinkedIn says the rollout will be gradual and vary by region and language, so not all users will see the changes immediately. Separately, LinkedIn is now displaying longer previews of text posts in the main feed before the "see more" cutoff kicks in, a shift that could boost engagement for creators and may also undercut the old "broetry" formatting trick, where posters used line breaks to hide their main point and bait clicks, since more text will now be visible upfront.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn is testing a redesigned navigation menu that consolidates desktop and mobile function listings, merging profile, analytics, saved posts and settings under one tab, plus a new "More" tab for games, news, groups, events and video.

articles.title: YouTube tests reduced payment threshold for creators
articles.summary: YouTube has begun experimenting with a reduced minimum payment threshold for its Partner Program, allowing a randomly selected group of creators in the U.S., India, and Indonesia to cash out earnings once they hit $20, rather than waiting to reach the standard $100 minimum. The change takes effect with October 2026 payments, and any unused balance below the new threshold will simply carry over to the following month. Creators included in the test will get a notification and can monitor updated payment activity through YouTube Studio on mobile; those who'd rather stick with a higher payout threshold can adjust their preference manually in AdSense for YouTube. The move comes as Instagram ramps up its own long-form video push, positioning itself as a stronger competitor for both viewers and creators. Since YouTube's monetization infrastructure remains more mature than Instagram's, lowering the payout bar could help it retain smaller or newer creators by giving them faster, more flexible access to ad revenue, reinforcing its advantage as rival platforms try to lure talent away.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is testing a lower Partner Program payout threshold of $20 (down from $100) for a randomly selected group of creators in the U.S., India, and Indonesia starting with October 2026 payments.

articles.title: Publicis installs leadership atop Marcel as agentic drives growth plans
articles.summary: Publicis Groupe has created a dedicated leadership team for Marcel, its internal AI tool launched in 2017, appointing existing executives Scott Hagedorn as CEO and Sam Levine Archer as chief strategy officer. Both joined Publicis four years ago from Omnicom, where they had run the media division; Hagedorn previously served as chief solutions architect and Archer as chief solutions officer. In their new roles, they'll expand Marcel's capabilities in influencer and creator marketing, sports, cultural trends, and optimizing content for AI chatbot answers, drawing on data from Publicis Sapient, Epsilon and Lotame. The move reflects Publicis' "Power of One" strategy of cross-agency collaboration and its heavy investment in data infrastructure, including last year's Lotame acquisition, which gave the company visibility into nearly 4 billion consumer profiles, and a pending $2.2 billion acquisition of ad-tech firm LiveRamp. CEO Arthur Sadoun has emphasized the company is increasing investment in data and technology while rivals cut back. Publicis posted 5% organic net revenue growth in Q3, though its Sapient technology division continues facing slower growth amid uneven enterprise AI adoption.
articles.li_summary: Publicis Groupe named Scott Hagedorn as CEO and Sam Levine Archer as chief strategy officer of its internal AI platform Marcel, aiming to expand agentic AI capabilities in influencer marketing, sports, culture and AI chatbot optimization.

articles.title: Pinterest strengthens bid to media buyers with programmatic solution
articles.summary: Pinterest rolled out a new programmatic advertising solution called Programmatic Deals on October 26, initially available across North America, South America and Asia Pacific. The offering lets media buyers purchase Pinterest's display and video ad inventory through supply-side platform Magnite (and Google Ad Manager in Latin America and Asia Pacific), alongside demand-side platforms Amazon Ads DVA+, Google Display & Video 360 and Yahoo DSP. The launch builds on a June test with beauty brand Moroccanoil, which added Pinterest to an existing campaign via Magnite and Amazon Ads, resulting in 15% higher incremental reach, just 1% audience overlap, 63% more new-to-brand buyers, and a 20% higher click-through rate versus the brand's typical video and display campaigns. This follows Pinterest's February acquisition of connected TV ad platform TvScientific, whose CEO Jason Fairchild now runs Pinterest's programmatic and affiliate operations, plus last May's hiring of Chip Jessop, formerly of Amazon, as the company's first head of programmatic. Pinterest reports 640 million monthly active users and over 80 billion monthly searches, more than half commercial. Q2 revenue hit $1.18 billion, up 18% year-over-year, with Q3 earnings due October 29.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest launched Programmatic Deals on Oct. 26 in North America, South America and Asia Pacific, letting media buyers purchase its display and video inventory through Magnite, Google DV360, Yahoo DSP and Amazon Ads DVA+.

articles.title: Australia’s proposed algorithmic opt-out gets pushback
articles.summary: Australia is in preliminary stages of drafting legislation, the Digital Duty of Care, that would require social media platforms to let users permanently disable algorithmic recommendations and default to feeds showing only accounts they've chosen to follow. Communications Minister Annika Wells argued at the National Press Club that engagement-driven algorithms prioritize attachment over user wellbeing and that platforms currently make opt-out settings deliberately hard to find or maintain. The push cites research, including an August University of Texas study and a 2025 International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science paper, linking algorithmic feeds to addictive behavior, depression, and dopamine disruption resembling substance addiction. Instagram chief Adam Mosseri has pushed back twice, including a recent Threads post, warning that removing recommendation algorithms would shrink Instagram's usage and reduce reach for creators as the "pie" of engagement gets smaller. Critics, including US commentator Michael Shellenberger at a Brisbane CPAC event, have alleged the bill could hand Australia's eSafety Commissioner excessive power over speech, including running fake accounts, though the article disputes those specific claims as misleading.
articles.li_summary: Australia's government, led by Communications Minister Annika Wells, is exploring Digital Duty of Care legislation forcing platforms like Instagram to offer a genuine opt-out from algorithmic feeds, defaulting instead to chronological updates from accounts users explicitly follow.

articles.title: More than half of US adults use social media to get their news
articles.summary: A new Pew Research report released October 23, based on a June survey of more than 3,500 U.S. adults, shows that 58% of Americans now view social media as an important way to stay informed about news and current events, up sharply from 43% in a comparable 2022 study. More strikingly, 13% now say social platforms are their single most important news source, compared to just 5% three years ago, which translates to roughly 35 million U.S. adults relying primarily on social apps for information, using Annie E. Casey Foundation population estimates. The findings highlight the growing power social platforms hold over public discourse and election-related information flow, reviving debates about content moderation and alleged censorship, including the State Department's December action against groups accused of pressuring platforms to suppress certain viewpoints. The report also revisits Mark Zuckerberg's shifting stance: in 2021 he warned that unchecked engagement-driven algorithms amplify sensationalist content and fuel polarization, yet by January 2025 he reversed course, loosening Meta's fact-checking and content rules around topics like immigration and gender identity despite acknowledging the risks.
articles.li_summary: Pew Research's October 23 survey of 3,500+ U.S. adults found 58% now consider social media an important news source, up from 43% in 2022, with 13% (roughly 35 million adults) calling it their primary source.

articles.title: TikTok playbook outlines the value of its high-end ad options
articles.summary: TikTok has published a new 12-page advertising playbook explaining how marketers can leverage its premium placement tools, TopView and Pulse Suite, to amplify holiday and seasonal campaigns. TopView guarantees advertisers the top slot in a user's feed for the day, maximizing first impressions, while Pulse Suite offers several tiers—Pulse Premiere pairs ads with top publisher content, and Pulse Core, Pulse Mentions, and Pulse Tastemakers align promotions with trending or popular posts. The guide includes engagement data tied to major cultural moments like the Super Bowl and the FIFA World Cup final, showing spikes in TikTok usage that brands could exploit through these premium placements. It also highlights seasonal patterns around the end-of-year and New Year period as high-engagement windows worth targeting. However, according to reporting from Stackmatix, these premium options aren't cheap—TopView campaigns start at roughly $50,000 for a single day, with Pulse Suite placements priced similarly—making them realistic only for larger advertisers with substantial budgets aiming for maximum reach during pivotal cultural or shopping moments.
articles.li_summary: TikTok released a 12-page advertising playbook detailing how brands can use its premium TopView and Pulse Suite ad placements—costing at least $50,000 per day—to boost visibility during major cultural events and holiday campaigns.

articles.title: Pinterest introduces new programmatic buying partnership
articles.summary: Pinterest has rolled out a new programmatic advertising partnership designed to make its ad inventory available through third-party buying platforms, rather than requiring advertisers to run Pinterest-specific campaigns. Facilitated by Magnite, the new offering, called Programmatic Deals, lets advertisers purchase selected Pinterest display and video inventory alongside their other campaigns through major supply-side and demand-side platforms, including Yahoo DSP, Amazon Ads DVA+ and Google Display and Video 360. This means ads bought through these external platforms can now appear in relevant Pinterest placements automatically, integrating Pinterest into the planning, buying and measurement workflows that many enterprise marketers already rely on. For Pinterest, the move opens a potentially significant new revenue stream by exposing its inventory to a much broader pool of programmatic buyers, while also giving the company a chance to showcase its platform's advertising performance to brands that may not have previously considered it. Programmatic Deals are currently live in North America, South America and Asia Pacific, with Pinterest directing interested advertisers to reach out to its sales representatives for more details on access and setup.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest launched Programmatic Deals via Magnite, letting advertisers buy its display and video inventory through Yahoo DSP, Amazon Ads DVA+ and Google Display and Video 360 across North America, South America and Asia Pacific.

articles.title: Edits comes to iPhone Duo and desktop
articles.summary: Meta rolled out two updates to its Edits video editing app this week. The first is a version built specifically for Apple's iPhone Duo foldable, letting users view their editing timeline and preview side by side thanks to the device's larger, adaptive screen; Meta says the interface adjusts around the phone's crease so editing stays usable in different folded positions. Separately, creator Taylor Golub posted a screenshot revealing Meta's in-development desktop version of Edits, which is now in limited live testing with select creators after being first announced back in June. The desktop layout gives users a wider view of editing tools and timeline elements on one screen, aiming to streamline how the app's various creation features work together. Instagram head Adam Mosseri responded to Golub's post, saying he sees the desktop build as a foundation Meta can expand on with many additional features going forward, suggesting Edits' desktop rollout is still early but central to the app's longer-term roadmap.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched a dedicated iPhone Duo version of its Edits video app with a foldable-friendly interface, while also testing a new desktop version that Instagram chief Adam Mosseri says will anchor future feature development.

articles.title: X provides holiday campaign tips
articles.summary: X held a webinar last week sharing holiday advertising guidance for marketers, emphasizing that attention and shopping intent peak simultaneously on the platform while users remain unusually receptive to brand messaging during this period. The company presented data on last year's holiday shopping engagement trends, peak activity windows, and audience demographics to help advertisers time campaigns effectively. X also addressed the growing role of AI in shopping decisions, advising brands to describe their products in plain, comparable language so AI models can easily summarize and recommend them. For ad creative, X recommended keeping copy to 50-100 characters (roughly one sentence), writing in a conversational tone rather than overselling, and using urgency tactics like limited-time offers paired with clear calls to action. The platform also advised eliminating distractions that pull focus from the primary conversion goal, directing traffic to a single destination like a website or app. Notably, X said advertisers should avoid tagging other accounts, since tags offer an "exit" from the ad, and confirmed that hashtags and multiple emojis remain prohibited in paid ads for similar reasons.
articles.li_summary: X hosted a webinar last week offering holiday campaign guidance, recommending 50-100 character ads, plain-language product descriptions for AI discoverability, and avoiding tags, hashtags, and multiple emojis in ads.

articles.title: TikTok US shares Q2 account enforcement data
articles.summary: TikTok's U.S.-based management arm, TikTok USDS, released its second Platform Security and Community Guidelines Report, covering April through June 2025, following its first report in July for Q1. The data shows sharp increases in enforcement activity: 14.6 million fake accounts removed, 64.8 million spam accounts blocked before creation, 781.4 million fake followers deleted, and 403.2 million fraudulent follow requests prevented. Video takedowns and livestream warnings or demonetizations also rose compared to Q1. The leading cause for video removal was violations involving regulated goods and services—covering drugs, alcohol, gambling, counterfeit items, risky financial products, and services selling fake engagement—followed by sexualized content and body exposure, consistent with prior-quarter trends. TikTok also reported disrupting 30 covert influence operations designed to manipulate public opinion, leading to the removal of more than 76,000 accounts and 4.8 million posts. This enforcement push comes as TikTok ramps up election-integrity efforts ahead of the U.S. midterms, including a newly announced Election Mission Control Center to monitor and respond to emerging manipulation risks amid ongoing scrutiny of its U.S. ownership structure.
articles.li_summary: TikTok USDS's second quarterly enforcement report (April 1–June 30) shows it removed 14.6 million fake accounts, blocked 64.8 million spam account creations, deleted 781.4 million fake followers, and dismantled 30 covert influence networks linked to over 76,000 accounts.

articles.title: Meta says advertisers should let campaigns gather data
articles.summary: Meta released a holiday season best-practices guide advising advertisers to stop tweaking ad campaigns prematurely and instead give its ad system sufficient time and data to optimize performance. The guide stresses treating each campaign setup like a detailed brief, with clearly defined optimization goals, budgets, bid strategies, and attribution settings from the outset. Meta's key data point: ad sets generating fewer than roughly 50 conversions per week ran about 28% more expensive per purchase, since the algorithm lacks enough signal to target efficiently below that volume. The company also cited last year's shopping trends, noting 42% of consumers said they'd planned to cut holiday spending, yet overall spend rose 4.2% year over year. Meta recommends using A/B testing or Conversion Lift studies to properly evaluate results rather than making reactive changes based on early dashboard fluctuations. The overall message asks marketers to trust Meta's automated systems more and intervene less, arguing that clear upfront instructions and patience—rather than constant monitoring—drive stronger peak-season campaign outcomes.
articles.li_summary: Meta's new holiday best-practices guide urges advertisers to resist adjusting campaigns too quickly, recommending at least 50 conversions per week per ad set, since underperforming sets below that threshold cost about 28% more per purchase.

articles.title: Meta delays business terms update over data scraping concerns
articles.summary: Meta has delayed its updated commercial terms of service, originally set to take effect Oct 30, pushing the launch to Nov 20 after backlash from publishers, advertisers, and regulators. The dispute centers on language permitting Meta to use bots, crawlers, and automated tools to access and periodically pull data from any domain or webpage connected to a business's use of Facebook or Instagram, then use that content to develop, train, and maintain its products. Critics, including the European Publishers Council and the UK's Competition and Markets Authority, warned this could effectively authorize Meta to scrape virtually any business website for AI training purposes. Meta called the backlash a misunderstanding, insisting the terms merely consolidate existing language for clarity and aren't tied to AI training; last week it already revised the wording to remove explicit training references. The company faces existing lawsuits over alleged use of copyrighted material to train its AI models, which intensified scrutiny of this update. Meta says businesses can still block crawlers via robots.txt files and that existing legal protections remain intact, but it now must explain the terms further to EU and UK authorities before relaunching.
articles.li_summary: Meta postponed its updated commercial terms of service from Oct 30 to Nov 20 after publishers, advertisers, and EU/UK regulators warned the language could let it scrape data from any business website using Facebook or Instagram.
